glab.instructions:
GitLab CLI MCP Server - Provides access to GitLab functionality through glab commands.

General Usage:
- Use --help flag with any tool to get detailed usage information
- For large outputs, use limit/offset parameters for pagination
- Check 'total_size' in response metadata to navigate results
- Most tools support common flags like --output for formatting

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Search once with a focused query describing what the code does or its name.

Write queries using function/class names or behavior descriptions, not error messages.
Returns file paths and line numbers — navigate directly there, do not repeat the search.
Pass a git URL or local path as `repo`; indexes are cached for the session.

query.description: Natural language or code query.
query.title: Query

repo.description: A local directory path or https:// or http:// git URL (e.g. https://github.com/org/repo) to index and search. The index is cached after the first call, so repeat queries are fast.
repo.title: Repo

max_snippet_lines.description: Lines of source to include per result. Default (10): function/class signature + first body lines, enough to confirm the location. 0: file path and line range only. None: full chunk (~10-20 lines). If the snippet does not contain enough context to confirm you have the right location, call again with max_snippet_lines=None.
max_snippet_lines.title: Max Snippet Lines

content.description: Content to search. Defaults to the MCP server's configured content.
content.title: Content

tools.name: find_related
tools.description:
Find code similar to a known location.

Useful for discovering all implementations of an interface, all callers of a function,
or all tests for a class. Use after `search` when you need related code beyond the primary result.
Pass `file_path` and `line` from a prior search result.

file_path.description: Path to the file as stored in the index (use file_path from a search result).
file_path.title: File Path

repo.description: A local directory path or https:// or http:// git URL (e.g. https://github.com/org/repo) to index and search. The index is cached after the first call, so repeat queries are fast.
repo.title: Repo

top_k.description: Number of similar chunks to return.
top_k.title: Top K

max_snippet_lines.description: Lines of source per result. Default 10 = signature + first body lines. 0 = location only. None = full chunk.
max_snippet_lines.title: Max Snippet Lines

content.description: Content containing the related file. Defaults to the MCP server configuration.
content.title: Content

semble.instructions: Instant code search for any local or remote git repository. Call `search` once with a focused query, it returns the file path and exact line. Navigate directly to that file at the given line; do not grep for the same content. Use `find_related` to discover similar code elsewhere in the same repo. When working in a local project, pass the project root as `repo`. For remote repos, pass an explicit https:// URL. Never guess or infer URLs.

tools.description:
Manage Grafana alerting routing configuration, including notification policies, contact points and time intervals.

Notification policies define how alerts are grouped, routed, and which contact points receive them.
Time intervals define active/mute periods for alert notifications.

When to use:
- Understanding how alerts are routed to contact points/receivers
- Debugging why an alert went to a specific receiver
- Checking grouping, timing, or mute interval settings

When NOT to use:
- Checking alert rule configuration or state (use alerting_manage_rules)

Manage Grafana alert rules with full CRUD capabilities and filtering.

When to use:
- Understanding why an alert is or isn't firing
- Auditing alert rule configuration (queries, conditions, labels, notification settings)
- Finding alert rules by state, folder, group, or name

- Comparing rule versions to see what changed

When NOT to use:

Each object has: datasourceUid (string, required), model (object with expr for data queries or type/expression/conditions for expressions), refId (string, auto-assigned if omitted), relativeTimeRange ({from, to} in seconds, defaults to {from:600,to:0}). For server-side expressions use datasourceUid '__expr__'. Example: [{datasourceUid: 'prometheus', model: {expr: 'up == 0'}}, {datasourceUid: '__expr__', model: {type: 'threshold', expression: 'A', conditions: [{evaluator: {type: 'gt', params: [0]}}]}}]

tools.name: alerting_manage_silences
tools.description:
Manage Grafana alerting silences. A silence temporarily suppresses notifications for alerts whose labels match a set of matchers, without changing the alert rules themselves.

Operations:
- 'list': list existing silences. Optionally filter by rule_uid (matches the __alert_rule_uid__ label) or by matchers.
- 'get': retrieve a single silence by silence_id.
- 'create': create a new silence. Requires matchers, starts_at, ends_at (RFC3339) and comment.
- 'update': modify an existing silence by silence_id. Requires matchers, starts_at, ends_at and comment. The id is only kept when the posted matchers and starts_at match the stored ones, so pass back the starts_at returned by 'get'; otherwise Alertmanager expires the old silence and returns a new id.
- 'delete': expire/remove a silence by silence_id.

When to use:
- Muting noisy or expected alerts during maintenance windows
- Inspecting or cleaning up existing silences

When NOT to use:
- Changing alert rule configuration or state (use alerting_manage_rules)
- Changing how alerts are routed to receivers (use alerting_manage_routing)

operation.description: The operation to perform: 'list' to list silences, 'get' to retrieve a silence by id, 'create' to create a new silence, 'update' to modify an existing silence by id, 'delete' to expire a silence by id

tools.name: query_loki_logs
tools.description: Executes a log query against a Loki or VictoriaLogs datasource and returns matching log entries (or metric samples on Loki). Defaults to the last hour, a limit of 10 entries, and 'backward' direction (newest first). The `logql` parameter takes LogQL on Loki and LogsQL on VictoriaLogs (e.g., Loki: `{app="foo"} |= "error"`; VictoriaLogs: `{app="foo"} "error"`). To count matching log lines precisely, use a `count_over_time()` metric query with queryType='instant'. Prefer using `query_loki_stats` first to cheaply check whether a stream contains data (avoiding expensive queries against empty streams) and `list_loki_label_names` / `list_loki_label_values` to verify labels exist before querying. Note: `query_loki_stats` returns approximate storage-level counts, not exact log line counts. For broad queries that match many lines, set `format` to 'compact' to group results by stream and avoid repeating label metadata on every line. If this server enables the Loki cost guardrail, expensive queries are rejected before execution: query cost is bytes SCANNED, determined only by the stream selector and time range — line filters (|=) and parsers (| json) reduce what is returned, not what is scanned. Use a stream selector with at least one selective positive label matcher (never `{}`, `=~".*"`/`=~".+"`, or negative-only matchers), keep time ranges narrow, and check size with `query_loki_stats` first; rejected queries return rewrite guidance.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

direction.description: Optionally, the direction of the query: 'forward' (oldest first) or 'backward' (newest first, default)

endRfc3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now')

format.description: Output format for log (streams) queries: 'full' (default) returns every entry with its own label metadata; 'compact' groups lines by stream so each label set is emitted only once (and per-line structured/parsed metadata is dropped), substantially reducing response size for broad queries. Ignored for metric queries.

limit.description: Optionally, the maximum number of log lines to return (default max: 100, configurable by MCP server).

logql.description: The LogQL query to execute against Loki. This can be a simple label matcher or a complex query with filters, parsers, and expressions. Supports full LogQL syntax including label matchers, filter operators, pattern expressions, and pipeline operations.

queryType.description: Query type: 'range' (default) or 'instant'. Instant queries return a single value at one point in time. Range queries return values over a time window. Use 'instant' for metric queries when you want the current value.

startRfc3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h')

stepSeconds.description: Resolution step in seconds for range metric queries. When running metric queries with queryType='range', this controls the time resolution of the returned data points.

Returns a list of patterns, each containing a pattern string and a total count of occurrences. Patterns help identify common log structures and anomalies. The `logql` parameter must be a stream selector (e.g., `{job="nginx"}`) and does not support line filters or aggregations. Defaults to the last hour if the time range is omitted. **Not supported on VictoriaLogs** datasources - use a `| stats` pipeline instead.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

endRfc3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now') (defaults to now)

startRfc3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h') (defaults to 1 hour ago)

tools.name: query_loki_stats
tools.description: Retrieves index-level statistics about log streams matching a given selector within a Loki or VictoriaLogs datasource and time range. Returns an object containing the count of streams, chunks, entries, and total bytes (e.g., `{"streams": 5, "chunks": 50, "entries": 10000, "bytes": 512000}`). **Important**: the `entries` count reflects storage-level index entries (chunk metadata), NOT the number of individual log lines matching the selector. To count actual matching log lines, use `query_loki_logs` with a `count_over_time()` metric query instead. On VictoriaLogs only `entries` is populated; the other fields remain zero. The `logql` parameter **must** be a simple label selector (e.g., `{app="nginx", env="prod"}`) and does not support line filters, parsers, or aggregations. Defaults to the last hour if the time range is omitted.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

endRfc3339.description: Optionally, the end time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now')

logql.description: The LogQL matcher expression to execute. This parameter only accepts label matcher expressions and does not support full LogQL queries. Line filters, pattern operations, and metric aggregations are not supported by the stats API endpoint. Only simple label selectors can be used here.

startRfc3339.description: Optionally, the start time of the query in RFC3339 format or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h')

tools.name: query_prometheus
tools.description: WORKFLOW: list_prometheus_metric_names -> list_prometheus_label_values -> query_prometheus. Query a PromQL-compatible datasource (Prometheus, Thanos, Mimir, Cloud Monitoring, etc.) using a PromQL expression. Supports instant queries (single point) and range queries (time range). Time: RFC3339 or relative expressions like 'now'\, 'now-1h'.

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

endTime.description: The end time. Supported formats are RFC3339 or relative to now (e.g. 'now', 'now-1.5h', 'now-2h45m'). Valid time units are 'ns', 'us' (or 'µs'), 'ms', 's', 'm', 'h', 'd'.

projectName.description: GCP project name to query (Cloud Monitoring datasources only). Overrides or substitutes the defaultProject configured on the datasource.

queryType.description: The type of query to use. Either 'range' or 'instant'

startTime.description: The start time. Required if queryType is 'range', ignored if queryType is 'instant' Supported formats are RFC3339 or relative to now (e.g. 'now', 'now-1.5h', 'now-2h45m'). Valid time units are 'ns', 'us' (or 'µs'), 'ms', 's', 'm', 'h', 'd'.

stepSeconds.description: The time series step size in seconds. Required if queryType is 'range', ignored if queryType is 'instant'

tools.name: query_prometheus_histogram
tools.description:
Query Prometheus histogram percentiles. DISCOVER FIRST: Use list_prometheus_metric_names with regex='.*_bucket$' to find histograms.

Generates histogram_quantile PromQL. Example: metric='http_duration', percentile=95, labels='job="api"'

Time formats: 'now-1h', '2026-02-02T19:00:00Z', '1738519200000' (Unix ms)

datasourceUid.description: The UID of the Prometheus datasource

endTime.description: End time (default: now). Supports RFC3339, relative, or Unix ms.

projectName.description: GCP project name to query (Cloud Monitoring datasources only). Overrides or substitutes the defaultProject configured on the datasource.

startTime.description: Start time (default: now-1h). Supports RFC3339, relative (now-1h), or Unix ms.

stepSeconds.description: Step size in seconds for range query (default: 60)

tools.name: query_pyroscope
tools.description:
Unified Pyroscope query tool for fetching profiles or metrics from Pyroscope. Profile data shows WHICH functions consume resources; metrics data
shows WHEN consumption spiked. Use query_type="both" for complete analysis in one call.

query_type options (extends Grafana's PyroscopeQueryType):
- "profile": returns profile data (shape controlled by format)
- "metrics": returns time-series data points
- "both" (default): returns both profile and metrics in one response

format options (shape of the profile data):
- "table" (default): per-function table with flat (self) and cumulative values, ranked by flat
- "dot": call graph in Graphviz DOT format; nodes are per source line, so one function may span several nodes

data_source_uid.description: The UID of the datasource to query

end_rfc_3339.description: End time in RFC3339 or relative time (e.g. 'now') (defaults to now)

format.description: Profile output format: "table" (default) for a per-function flat/cum table, or "dot" for a call graph in Graphviz DOT format

group_by.description: Labels to group metrics series by

max_node_depth.description: Max functions in the profile table or nodes in the call graph; it is a count, not a depth (default: 100)

profile_type.description: The profile type, use list_pyroscope_profile_types to discover available types

query_type.description: Query type: "profile" (flamegraph), "metrics" (time-series), or "both" (default). Use "both" for complete analysis

start_rfc_3339.description: Start time in RFC3339 or relative time (e.g. 'now-1h') (defaults to 1 hour ago)

step.description: Seconds between metrics data points (default: auto)

tools.name: search_dashboards
tools.description: Search for Grafana dashboards by a query string. Returns a list of matching dashboards with details like title, UID, folder, tags, and URL.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (max 100)

query.description: The query to search for

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search Grafana documentation. Returns matching pages with title, URL, description, and product. Call with no query to list available product groups.

product.description: Filter results to a specific product (e.g. 'Grafana Tempo', 'Grafana Loki')

query.description: Search query for Grafana documentation. Omit to list all available product groups.

tools.name: search_folders
tools.description: Search for Grafana folders by a query string. Returns matching folders with details like title, UID, and URL.

query.description: The query to search for

tools.name: search_plugin_information
tools.description: Search the Grafana plugin catalog by keyword to discover available plugins before installing or getting plugin details on a specific instance. Returns results sorted by trust: official Grafana Labs plugins first, then commercial partner plugins, then community plugins. Use this tool when a user describes a plugin by purpose or partial name (e.g. 'azure monitoring', 'loki', 'database') — it returns the exact pluginId to pass to get_plugin or install_plugin. Results include warnings for enterprise-only or Angular-based plugins.

query.description: Keyword to search for plugins (e.g. 'azure', 'prometheus', 'loki', 'database'). Matches against plugin name, slug, description, and keywords.

tools.name: suggest_loki_alloy_label_config
tools.description: Generates an Alloy loki.process snippet enforcing an approved label set via stage.label_keep, with optional log-level normalisation and soft-enforcement placeholders.

approvedLabels.description: Labels to keep on the index.

requiredLabels.description: Labels that get an 'unknown' placeholder when missing.

tools.name: update_alert_group
tools.description: Update the state of a Grafana OnCall alert group: acknowledge, unacknowledge, resolve, or unresolve it by ID. Returns the alert group's resulting OnCall state (one of new, acknowledged, resolved, silenced), or a stateWarning explaining why that state could not be read back after a successful update.

alertGroupId.description: The ID of the alert group to update

state.description: New state for the alert group. One of: acknowledged, unacknowledged, resolved, unresolved

tools.name: update_annotation
tools.description: Updates the provided properties of an annotation by ID. Only fields included in the request are modified; omitted fields are left unchanged.

tools.name: update_dashboard
tools.description: Create or update a dashboard. Two modes: (1) Full JSON — provide 'dashboard' for new dashboards or complete replacements. (2) Patch — provide 'uid' + 'operations' to make targeted changes to an existing dashboard. One of these two modes is required; 'folderUid'\, 'message'\, and 'overwrite' are supplementary and do nothing on their own. Dashboard authoring guidance: if a saved query must support one\, many\, or All values from a multi-select variable inside a regex expression or matcher\, save '${var:regex}' rather than plain '$var'. Saved dashboard annotation queries/definitions must be written into dashboard JSON under 'annotations.list'; the create_annotation tool creates annotation events and does not add a reusable dashboard annotation query/definition to the saved dashboard. For stat panels over the current dashboard range\, make the query return the range-level result the stat should display; panel-side reduction only reduces returned series and does not compute peak-over-range or ratio-of-peaks semantics for you. Patch operations support JSONPaths like '$.panels[0].targets[0].expr'\, '$.panels[1].title'\, '$.panels[2].targets[0].datasource'\, '$.templating.list/-'\, and '$.annotations.list/-'. Append to arrays with '/- ' syntax: '$.panels/- '. Remove by index: {"op": "remove"\, "path": "$.panels[2]"}. Multiple removes on the same array are automatically reordered to avoid index-shifting issues. Note: only numeric array indices are supported in patch paths; filter expressions like [?(@.id==2)] and wildcards like [*] are not supported. v2 dashboards (check 'isV2' from get_dashboard_by_uid) use a different shape: patch '$.elements.<name>.spec.title' or '$.elements.<name>.spec.data.spec.queries[0].spec' and edit '$.variables'/'$.layout' rather than '$.panels'/'$.templating.list'. Full-JSON saves containing top-level 'elements'/'layout' are written as v2 and require a Kubernetes-capable Grafana. After creating or updating a dashboard\, verify that panel queries return data by using `run_panel_query` or the appropriate query tool (`query_prometheus`\, `query_loki_logs`\, etc.) to validate expressions before considering the task complete.

dashboard.description: The full dashboard JSON. Use for creating new dashboards or complete updates. Saved dashboard annotation queries/definitions live in 'annotations.list' inside this JSON; they are different from annotation events created with create_annotation. Large dashboards consume significant context - consider using patches for small changes.

folderUid.description: The UID of the dashboard's folder

message.description: Set a commit message for the version history

path.description: JSONPath to the property to modify. Supports: '$.title', '$.panels[0].title', '$.panels[0].targets[0].expr', '$.panels[1].targets[0].datasource', '$.templating.list/-' (append a variable), '$.annotations.list/-' (append a saved dashboard annotation query/definition). For appending to arrays, use '/- ' syntax: '$.panels/- ' (append to panels array) or '$.panels[2]/- ' (append to nested array at index 2).

value.description: New value for replace/add operations. When adding a saved dashboard annotation query/definition, append an object to '$.annotations.list' rather than calling create_annotation.

operations.description: Array of patch operations for targeted updates. More efficient than full dashboard JSON for small changes. Common paths: '$.templating.list/-' to add a variable, '$.annotations.list/-' to add a saved dashboard annotation query/definition, '$.panels[0].targets[0].expr' to replace a panel query.

overwrite.description: Overwrite the dashboard if it exists. Otherwise create one

uid.description: UID of existing dashboard to update. Must be used together with 'operations'. Providing 'uid' without 'operations' will fail.

userId.description: ID of the user making the change

tools.name: update_datasource
tools.description: Update non-secret datasource fields by UID. Omitted fields are preserved. IMPORTANT: always call this tool twice. First call: provide only the uid — the tool returns the datasource's field schema. After receiving the schema, ask the user which fields they want to change and confirm each new value; do not infer or reset fields the user did not mention. Second call: provide the uid, schemaReviewed=true, and the changed values in the fields map. Returns an update message and a health check. For secrets, direct the user to the Grafana UI.

fields.description: Datasource field values to change, keyed by field key from the schema returned on the first call. The server uses each field's target (root or jsonData) to place values correctly, merging jsonData changes into the existing settings. Only include the fields you want to change. Example: {"httpMethod": "POST"}.

jsonData.description: Non-secret plugin settings; replaces existing jsonData when set

name.description: Display name

schemaReviewed.description: Set to true on the second call to confirm you reviewed the schema and collected the changes from the user.

uid.description: UID of the datasource to update

tools.name: update_incident
tools.description: Update an existing Grafana incident by ID. Allows changing the status ('active' or 'resolved'), the severity, the title, and custom field values. Only the provided fields are changed. Use this to resolve an incident, to correct its severity or title, or to fill in custom fields as part of an on-call workflow.

field.description: The name or UUID of the custom field to set. Use list_incident_custom_fields to discover the available fields

values.description: The value(s) to set. Text and number fields take a single value; single-select fields take one option; multi-select fields take one or more options. Select options may be given as their label, value or UUID. Pass an empty list to clear the field

customFields.description: Custom field values to set. Only the listed fields are changed. Use list_incident_custom_fields to discover the available fields and their valid values

incidentId.description: The ID of the incident to update

severity.description: The new severity of the incident, e.g. 'minor', 'major', 'critical'

status.description: The new status of the incident. Valid values: 'active', 'resolved'

title.description: The new title of the incident

tools.name: user_info
tools.description: Get information about the current Grafana identity: login, email, name, whether it is a Grafana (server) admin, the current organization, and the organizations it can access (with roles). Call this to discover which orgId values are valid before targeting a specific organization, and to understand the identity's capabilities.

tools.name: validate_provisioning_file
tools.description: Validate a file in a provisioning repository at a given branch or commit by dry-run applying it. Returns whether the file would be accepted (valid)\, what resource action would result (create/update)\, the target resource type\, and any structured validation errors. Use to confirm a draft dashboard or other resource will be accepted before merging or applying a PR — this is the same validation surface that Grafana's PR commenter reports.

ref.description: Branch or commit SHA. Defaults to the repository's main branch.

repo.description: Provisioning repository slug. Get one from list_provisioning_repositories.

resources.name: Panel Viewer
resources.description: Interactive HTML viewer for Grafana panel images

grafana.instructions:
This server provides access to your Grafana instance and the surrounding ecosystem.

Available Capabilities:
- Search: Find dashboards, folders, and other Grafana resources.
- Datasources: List and fetch details for datasources.
- Incidents: Search, create, update, and resolve incidents in Grafana Incident.
- Prometheus: Run PromQL queries, retrieve metric metadata, and explore label names/values.
- Loki: Run LogQL queries, retrieve log metadata, and explore label names/values.
- Alerting: List and fetch alert rules and notification contact points.
- Dashboards: Search, retrieve, update, and create dashboards. Extract panel queries and datasource information.
- Folders: Manage dashboard folders.
- OnCall: View and manage on-call schedules, shifts, teams, and users.
- Asserts: Query and analyze assertion data.
- Sift Investigations: Start and manage Sift investigations, analyze logs/traces, find error patterns, and detect slow requests.
- Pyroscope: Profile applications and fetch profiling data.
- Navigation: Generate deeplink URLs for Grafana resources like dashboards, panels, and Explore queries, with optional built-in shortening.
- Annotations: Create and manage dashboard annotations.
- Rendering: Export dashboard panels or full dashboards as PNG images (requires Grafana Image Renderer plugin).
- Snapshots: List, get, create, and delete dashboard snapshots.
- Plugins: Check whether Grafana plugins are installed and fetch plugin details.
- API: Make authenticated HTTP requests to any Grafana API endpoint with optional jq-style response filtering.
- Config: Generate operator-facing configuration snippets (e.g. Alloy label-enforcement pipelines).
- Provisioning: List provisioning repositories (e.g. git-sync sources) to discover repository slugs for use with rendering tools.
- Docs: Search and retrieve Grafana product documentation (powered by grafana.com/llms-full.txt).
- User: Identify the current user/credential, its capabilities, and the organizations it can access.
- Proxied Tools: Access tools from external MCP servers (like Tempo) through dynamic discovery.

Timestamp parameters without a timezone offset are interpreted as UTC. Include an offset like '-05:00' or use relative syntax like 'now-1h' to query in a different timezone.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search the Capawesome documentation, guides and blog by keyword. Use this first for any question about Capawesome SDKs (Capacitor and Cordova plugins such as Live Update, NFC, Biometrics), Capawesome Cloud (live updates, native builds, app store publishing, automations), Capawesome Insiders or the Capawesome CLI — the answer is almost always documented, and guessing plugin APIs or CLI flags produces broken code. Returns the best matching page sections with `title`, `url`, `snippet`, `section` and, for a hit inside a page, the `parentTitle` and `parentUrl` of that page. The same results are attached as structured content. Do not use this to read a full page: call `get_doc_page` with a `url` from these results. Do not use it to browse recent announcements or release notes: use `list_blog_posts`. Do not use it for anything about a concrete app, build, channel or deployment in Capawesome Cloud: those live behind the `cloud_*` tools.

query.description: The search terms, e.g. "live update rollback" or "biometrics android setup". Plain keywords work best; no search operators are supported.

section.description: Restrict the search to one part of the documentation: "sdks" (plugin references and guides), "cloud" (Capawesome Cloud), "insiders" (Capawesome Insiders) or "blog" (articles and release notes). Defaults to searching everything.

limit.description: The maximum number of results to return, e.g. 5. Defaults to 10, maximum 25.

tools.name: get_doc_page
tools.description: Read the full source markdown of a Capawesome documentation or blog page. Use this after `search_docs` to read a page end to end before writing code against a plugin API, a CLI command or a Capawesome Cloud workflow — snippets from search results are deliberately short and regularly omit required configuration steps. Returns the page markdown including code samples, exactly as it is authored. Do not use this to find a page: it needs the exact URL or path, so run `search_docs` (or `list_blog_posts` for articles) first. Do not use it for pages outside capawesome.io.

url.description: The page URL or site-relative path, e.g. "https://capawesome.io/docs/cloud/live-updates/" or "cloud/live-updates/". Anchors are ignored; the whole page is returned.

tools.name: list_blog_posts
tools.description: List the 20 most recent posts from the Capawesome blog, newest first. Use this when the question is about what is new — recent releases, announcements, monthly updates, deprecations or newly published guides. Returns `title`, `description`, `date`, `categories` and `url` per post; pass a `url` to `get_doc_page` to read the whole article. Do not use this to answer a topic question: the feed only carries the newest posts, so search the documentation and the blog archive with `search_docs` instead.

tools.name: cloud_get_current_user
tools.description: Get the Capawesome Cloud user the provided token belongs to. Use this first to verify that the token works and to confirm whose account the following calls act on. It is the cheapest way to tell an invalid token apart from a permission problem. Returns `id`, `email`, `name`, `emailVerified`, `twoFactorEnabled`, `lastSeenAt` and the timestamps. Do not use this to list what the user can access: use `cloud_list_organizations`. The user profile cannot be changed through this server.

tools.name: cloud_list_organizations
tools.description: List the Capawesome Cloud organizations the token has access to. Use this at the start of almost every workflow: apps, jobs, teams, license keys and Git connections are all scoped to an organization, and their tools need the `organizationId` returned here. Returns `id`, `name`, `slug`, `countryAllowlist`, `ipAllowlist`, `twoFactorRequired` and the timestamps per organization. Do not use this to list apps (use `cloud_list_apps`) or members (use `cloud_list_members`).

tools.name: cloud_get_organization
tools.description: Get a single Capawesome Cloud organization by its id. Use this to check the security settings that can make otherwise valid calls fail: an IP or country allowlist blocks requests from outside it, and a two-factor requirement blocks members who have not enabled it. Returns `id`, `name`, `slug`, `countryAllowlist`, `ipAllowlist`, `twoFactorRequired`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. Do not use this to read billing or subscription details, which are not exposed through this server; open the Capawesome Cloud Console for those.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

tools.name: cloud_create_organization
tools.description: Create a new Capawesome Cloud organization. Use this when a team needs its own billing, members and apps — for most work an existing organization from `cloud_list_organizations` is the right place instead. A trial code, if you were given one, is redeemed during creation. Returns the created organization with `id`, `name` and `slug`; the caller becomes its owner. Do not use this to add someone to an existing organization (use `cloud_create_invitation`) or to create a team inside one (use `cloud_create_team`). Organizations cannot be deleted through this server.

name.description: The name of the organization, e.g. "Acme Inc.".

trialCode.description: A trial code to redeem while creating the organization, e.g. "TRIAL-2026". Optional.

tools.name: cloud_update_organization
tools.description: Update the name or the security settings of a Capawesome Cloud organization. Use this to rename an organization or to restrict API access to certain IP ranges or countries. Setting an allowlist that excludes your own address locks you out of the API, so verify the current address before applying one. Returns the updated organization. Do not use this to change a member's role or to manage billing: neither is exposed through this server. Requires an owner or admin role.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

name.description: The new name of the organization, e.g. "Acme Inc.". Optional.

countryAllowlist.description: The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes allowed to access the API, e.g. ["DE", "AT"]. Pass null to allow every country. Optional.

ipAllowlist.description: The IP addresses or CIDR ranges allowed to access the API, e.g. ["203.0.113.4/32"]. Pass null to allow every address. Optional.

twoFactorRequired.description: Whether members must have two-factor authentication enabled, e.g. true. Optional.

tools.name: cloud_list_members
tools.description: List the members of a Capawesome Cloud organization. Use this to see who has access and with which role, and to resolve an email address to the membership id that `cloud_delete_member` and `cloud_create_team` need. Returns `id` (the membership id), `userId`, `role`, the member's `user` with `email` and `name`, and `lastSeenAt` per member. Do not use this to list pending invitations (use `cloud_list_invitations`) or the members of a team (use `cloud_get_team` with `includeMembers`).

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

query.description: A free-text filter matching the membership id, user id or email, e.g. "@acme.com". Optional.

role.description: Return only members with this role, e.g. "admin". Optional.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return, e.g. 20. Defaults to 10, maximum 50.

offset.description: The number of items to skip, e.g. 10 to read the second page. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: cloud_delete_member
tools.description: Remove a member from a Capawesome Cloud organization. Use this when someone leaves the team: the member immediately loses access to every app of the organization, including through teams they belong to. Returns a confirmation. Do not use this to downgrade someone's permissions — role changes are not exposed through this server — and do not use it to revoke a pending invitation (use `cloud_delete_invitation`). Requires an owner or admin role.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

memberId.description: The id of the membership (not the user id), as returned by `cloud_list_members`.

tools.name: cloud_list_invitations
tools.description: List the invitations of a Capawesome Cloud organization. Use this to check whether an invitation is still pending, was accepted, or expired before sending another one. Returns `id`, `email`, `role`, `status` (`pending`, `accepted`, `canceled` or `rejected`), `inviterId`, `expiresAt` and the timestamps per invitation. Do not use this to list members who already joined (use `cloud_list_members`).

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

query.description: A free-text filter matching the invitation id or email, e.g. "jane@". Optional.

role.description: Return only invitations for this role, e.g. "member". Optional.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return, e.g. 20. Defaults to 10, maximum 50.

offset.description: The number of items to skip, e.g. 10 to read the second page. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: cloud_create_invitation
tools.description: Invite a user to a Capawesome Cloud organization by email. Use this to give someone access. The invitation is emailed and has to be accepted before the user shows up in `cloud_list_members`. Pick the smallest role that fits: `viewer` reads, `member` builds and deploys, `admin` also manages members and settings, `billing` manages the subscription. Returns the created invitation with `id`, `email`, `role`, `status` and `expiresAt`. Do not use this to change an existing member's role, which this server does not expose, and note that owners cannot be invited. Resending is not supported: revoke with `cloud_delete_invitation` and invite again.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

email.description: The email address to invite, e.g. "jane@acme.com".

role.description: The role the user receives after accepting, e.g. "member". Owners cannot be invited.

tools.name: cloud_delete_invitation
tools.description: Revoke a pending invitation of a Capawesome Cloud organization. Use this when an invitation was sent to the wrong address or is no longer wanted; the link stops working immediately. Returns a confirmation. Do not use this to remove someone who already accepted (use `cloud_delete_member`). Requires an owner or admin role.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

invitationId.description: The id of the invitation to revoke, as returned by `cloud_list_invitations`.

tools.name: cloud_create_app
tools.description: Create a new app in a Capawesome Cloud organization. Use this once per mobile app before configuring live updates, native builds or app store publishing. The returned `id` is the `appId` all other tools take. Returns the created app with `id`, `name`, `type` and `organizationId`. Do not use this to create an organization (use `cloud_create_organization`), a channel (`cloud_create_app_channel`) or an environment (`cloud_create_app_environment`). Apps cannot be deleted through this server.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

name.description: The name of the app, e.g. "Acme Mobile".

type.description: The framework the app is built with: "capacitor" or "cordova" for cross-platform apps, "android" or "ios" for pure native apps. Live updates require "capacitor" or "cordova".

tools.name: cloud_list_apps
tools.description: List the apps of a Capawesome Cloud organization. Use this to resolve an app name to the `appId` that nearly every other `cloud_*` tool needs. Pass `name` to filter by exact name, which returns the single match since app names are unique. Returns `id`, `name`, `type`, `organizationId`, the default `appChannelId` and `appEnvironmentId` and the timestamps per app. Do not use this to list organizations (use `cloud_list_organizations`) or to read one app you already have the id of (use `cloud_get_app`).

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

name.description: Filter by exact name, e.g. "production". Returns the single match, since names are unique. Optional.

query.description: A free-text filter matching the name or id, e.g. "production". Defaults to no filter.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return, e.g. 20. Defaults to 10, maximum 50.

offset.description: The number of items to skip, e.g. 10 to read the second page. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: cloud_get_app
tools.description: Get a single app of Capawesome Cloud by its id. Use this to check which channel and environment a build or deployment defaults to, or to confirm the app type before creating a build. Returns `id`, `name`, `type`, `organizationId`, `appChannelId` (default live update channel), `appEnvironmentId` (default environment), `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. Do not use this to search for an app by name: use `cloud_list_apps`.

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

tools.name: cloud_update_app
tools.description: Update the settings of an app in Capawesome Cloud. Use this to rename an app, to change the default channel or environment new builds and deployments fall back to, or to toggle channel discovery for the live update SDK. Returns the updated app. Do not use this to pause a channel (use `cloud_update_app_channel`), to set environment variables (use `cloud_update_app_environment`) or to link a Git repository (use `cloud_set_app_repository`).

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

name.description: The new name of the app, e.g. "Acme Mobile". Optional.

type.description: The framework the app is built with: "capacitor" or "cordova" for cross-platform apps, "android" or "ios" for pure native apps. Live updates require "capacitor" or "cordova". Optional.

appChannelId.description: The id of the channel devices use when they do not request a specific one. Pass null to clear it. Optional.

appEnvironmentId.description: The id of the environment builds use by default. Pass null to clear it. Optional.

appChannelDiscoveryEnabled.description: Whether devices may select a channel by name at runtime, e.g. true to let testers opt into a beta channel. Optional.

tools.name: cloud_list_app_channels
tools.description: List the live update channels of an app in Capawesome Cloud. Use this to resolve a channel name such as "production" or "beta" to its id, and to see at a glance which channels are paused and how many devices they serve. Returns `id`, `name`, `appDeploymentId` (the deployment currently served), `pausedAt` (null while active), `totalAppDeployments` and `totalAppDevices` per channel. Do not use this to list the deployments of a channel (use `cloud_list_app_deployments` with `appChannelId`) or the devices on it (use `cloud_list_app_devices`).

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

name.description: Return only the channel with this exact name, e.g. "production".

query.description: A free-text filter matching the name or id, e.g. "production". Defaults to no filter.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return, e.g. 20. Defaults to 10, maximum 50.

offset.description: The number of items to skip, e.g. 10 to read the second page. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: cloud_get_app_channel
tools.description: Get a single live update channel of an app in Capawesome Cloud. Use this to check which deployment a channel currently serves and whether it is paused before rolling out or rolling back an update. Returns `id`, `name`, `appId`, `appDeploymentId`, `pausedAt`, `totalAppDeployments`, `totalAppDevices` and the timestamps. Do not use this to find a channel by name: use `cloud_list_app_channels`.

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

channelId.description: The id of the channel, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_app_channels` to look it up by name.

tools.name: cloud_create_app_channel
tools.description: Create a live update channel for an app in Capawesome Cloud. Use this to separate audiences that should receive different bundles, e.g. a "production" channel for the App Store build and a "beta" channel testers opt into. A device receives the deployment of the channel it is assigned to. Returns the created channel with `id` and `name`; pass that `id` to `cloud_create_app_deployment` to publish a build to it. Do not use this to publish an update (use `cloud_create_app_deployment`) or to pause an existing channel (use `cloud_update_app_channel`).

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

name.description: The name of the channel, e.g. "production" or "beta".

expiresAt.description: The ISO 8601 date the channel stops serving updates, e.g. "2026-12-31T00:00:00.000Z". Defaults to never expiring.

protected.description: Whether the channel only serves code-signed bundles, e.g. true for production. Defaults to false.

tools.name: cloud_update_app_channel
tools.description: Rename a live update channel, change its expiry or protection, and pause or resume it. Use `paused: true` to stop a channel from serving updates immediately — the fastest way to stop a bad rollout while you prepare a fix. Use `paused: false` to resume it. Renaming a channel changes which devices resolve to it, so rename with care. Returns the applied changes; each requested change is dispatched separately and reported individually, so a partial failure names the step that failed. Do not use this to change which build a channel serves: create a new deployment with `cloud_create_app_deployment`, or deploy an earlier build to roll back. Do not use it to delete a channel (`cloud_delete_app_channel`).

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

channelId.description: The id of the channel, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_app_channels` to look it up by name.

name.description: The new name of the channel, e.g. "production". Optional.

expiresAt.description: The new ISO 8601 expiry date, e.g. "2026-12-31T00:00:00.000Z". Optional.

protected.description: Whether the channel only serves code-signed bundles, e.g. true. Optional.

paused.description: Pass true to pause the channel so devices stop receiving updates, false to resume it. Optional.

tools.name: cloud_delete_app_channel
tools.description: Permanently delete a live update channel of an app in Capawesome Cloud. Use this only to clean up a channel that is no longer needed. Devices assigned to the channel stop receiving live updates, and the channel's deployment history is lost. Identify the channel by `channelId` or by `name` — provide exactly one. Returns a confirmation. Do not use this to stop a rollout temporarily: pause the channel with `cloud_update_app_channel` instead, which is reversible.

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

channelId.description: The id of the channel to delete. Provide either `channelId` or `name`.

name.description: The name of the channel to delete, e.g. "production". Provide either `channelId` or `name`.

tools.name: cloud_list_app_builds
tools.description: List the builds of an app in Capawesome Cloud, newest first. Use this to find the `id` of a build you want to deploy, share or inspect — including the previous good build when you need to roll a channel back. Returns `id`, `platform`, `type`, `numberAsString` (the sequential build number), `jobId`, `appBuildArtifactId`, `packageName`, `packageVersion` and the timestamps per build. Do not use this to find out why a build failed (use `cloud_diagnose_job` with the build's `jobId`) or to list deployments (use `cloud_list_app_deployments`).

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

platform.description: The platform to build: "android", "ios", or "web" for the web assets a live update ships. Optional.

appGitCommit.description: Return only builds of this Git commit SHA, e.g. "9fceb02". Optional.

appAutomationId.description: Return only builds triggered by this automation id. Optional.

query.description: A free-text filter matching the name or id, e.g. "production". Defaults to no filter.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return, e.g. 20. Defaults to 10, maximum 50.

offset.description: The number of items to skip, e.g. 10 to read the second page. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: cloud_get_app_build
tools.description: Get a single build of an app in Capawesome Cloud, together with the status of its job and its downloadable artifacts. Use this to check whether a build succeeded and to hand a colleague a download link for the resulting APK, AAB or IPA. Returns the build fields (`id`, `platform`, `type`, `numberAsString`, `packageName`, `packageVersion`, `jobId`), the `jobStatus`, and per artifact its `id`, `type`, `status`, `totalSizeInBytes` and a signed, time-limited `downloadUrl`. Do not use this to find out why a build failed: pass its `jobId` to `cloud_diagnose_job`. Do not use it to create a public link for testers: use `cloud_create_app_build_share`.

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

buildId.description: The id of the build, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_app_builds` to look it up.

tools.name: cloud_create_app_build
tools.description: Start a build of an app in Capawesome Cloud from a Git reference or an uploaded source archive. The `platform` can be `android`, `ios` or `web` (more may be added over time); only `android` and `ios` produce native binaries. Use `gitRef` (branch, tag or commit) when the app has a linked repository, or `sourceArchiveUrl` when the sources were uploaded elsewhere. For live updates, build the `web` platform and then deploy the resulting build to a channel with `cloud_create_app_deployment` once its job succeeded — building alone ships nothing. For store releases, build `android` or `ios` with the matching certificate and deploy to a destination. Returns the created build with `id` and `jobId`; poll `cloud_get_app_build` or `cloud_get_job` until the job leaves `queued`/`in_progress`. Do not use this to upload a local folder: this server cannot upload files, so publish a live update by building from Git or an archive URL, or use the Capawesome CLI. Do not use it to deploy (use `cloud_create_app_deployment`) or to cancel a running build (use `cloud_cancel_job`).

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

platform.description: The platform to build: "android", "ios", or "web" for the web assets a live update ships.

gitRef.description: The branch, tag or commit to build, e.g. "main". Requires a linked repository; see `cloud_get_app_repository`.

sourceArchiveUrl.description: The URL of an already uploaded source archive (zip), e.g. "https://example.com/source.zip". Alternative to `gitRef`.

type.description: The build type, e.g. "app-store" for a store release or "ad-hoc" for internal distribution. Defaults to the platform default.

stack.description: The macOS build machine image, e.g. "macos-tahoe". Defaults to the organization default.

appCertificateId.description: The id of the signing certificate to use. Provide the id or the name (`appCertificateName`). Use `cloud_list_app_certificates` to look it up. Optional.

appCertificateName.description: The name of the signing certificate to use, e.g. "Acme Production". Ignored if `appCertificateId` is set. Optional.

appConfigurationId.description: The id of the app configuration overriding the native app id and name. Provide the id or the name (`appConfigurationName`). Optional.

appConfigurationName.description: The name of the app configuration to use, e.g. "staging". Ignored if `appConfigurationId` is set. Optional.

appEnvironmentId.description: The id of the environment providing variables and secrets to the build. Provide the id or the name (`appEnvironmentName`). Defaults to the app's default environment.

appEnvironmentName.description: The name of the environment to use, e.g. "staging". Ignored if `appEnvironmentId` is set. Optional.

appChannelId.description: The id of the live update channel the built app should subscribe to. Optional.

appDestinationId.description: The id of the app store destination the build is prepared for. Optional.

adHocEnvironmentVariables.description: Extra non-secret environment variables for this build only, e.g. { "API_URL": "https://staging.example.com" }. Do not pass secrets here; store them in an environment instead.

tools.name: cloud_create_app_build_share
tools.description: Create a public share link for a successful app build in Capawesome Cloud. Use this to hand testers or stakeholders a page where they can install the build without a Capawesome account — the link also works as a QR code for on-device installs. Calling it again for the same build returns the existing link instead of creating a second one. Returns `id`, `webUrl` (the public page), `qrCodeUrl` (a PNG of that page's link), `description` and `expiresAt`. Do not use this for builds whose job has not succeeded — the API rejects those. Do not use it to download an artifact yourself: `cloud_get_app_build` returns signed download URLs. Revoke a link with `cloud_delete_app_build_share`.

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

buildId.description: The id of the build, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_app_builds` to look it up.

description.description: A note shown on the share page, e.g. "Release candidate 1.4.0". Optional.

expiresAt.description: The ISO 8601 date the link stops working, e.g. "2026-12-31T00:00:00.000Z". Defaults to never expiring.

tools.name: cloud_delete_app_build_share
tools.description: Revoke the public share link of an app build in Capawesome Cloud. Use this as soon as a link should no longer be reachable — it stops working immediately, and anyone holding the URL or QR code loses access to the build. Returns a confirmation. Do not use this to delete the build itself; the build and its artifacts stay available to organization members.

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

buildId.description: The id of the build, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_app_builds` to look it up.

shareId.description: The id of the share to revoke, as returned by `cloud_create_app_build_share`.

tools.name: cloud_list_app_deployments
tools.description: List the deployments of an app in Capawesome Cloud, newest first. Use this to see the rollout history of a channel or store destination — and, before a rollback, to find the `appBuildId` of the build that was live before the current one. Returns `id`, `appBuildId`, `appChannelId`, `appDestinationId`, `jobId`, `rolloutPercentage` and the timestamps per deployment. Do not use this to list builds (use `cloud_list_app_builds`) or to inspect the progress of a running deployment (use `cloud_get_job` with the `jobId`).

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

appBuildId.description: Return only deployments of this build id. Optional.

appChannelId.description: Return only live update deployments to this channel id. Optional.

appDestinationId.description: Return only app store deployments to this destination id. Optional.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return, e.g. 20. Defaults to 10, maximum 50.

offset.description: The number of items to skip, e.g. 10 to read the second page. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: cloud_get_app_deployment
tools.description: Get a single deployment of an app in Capawesome Cloud, together with the status of the job processing it. Use this after `cloud_create_app_deployment` to check whether the rollout finished, is still running or failed. Returns the deployment fields (`id`, `appBuildId`, `appChannelId`, `appDestinationId`, `rolloutPercentage`, `jobId`) plus `jobStatus` and `jobFinishedAt` when a job is attached. Do not use this to read the failure reason of a failed deployment: pass its `jobId` to `cloud_diagnose_job`.

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

deploymentId.description: The id of the deployment, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_app_deployments` to look it up.

tools.name: cloud_create_app_deployment
tools.description: Deploy a build of an app in Capawesome Cloud — either as a live update to a channel, or to an app store destination. Pass `appChannelId` (or `appChannelName`) to publish the build's web assets as a live update, or `appDestinationId` (or `appDestinationName`) to submit the build to TestFlight or Google Play. This is also the rollback primitive: to roll a channel back, deploy the `appBuildId` of the last good build to the same channel — there is no separate rollback tool. Use `rolloutPercentage` to release gradually and raise it later with `cloud_update_app_deployment`. Returns the created deployment with `id`, `rolloutPercentage` and the `jobId` processing it; poll `cloud_get_app_deployment` or `cloud_get_job` for the outcome. Do not use this to create the build itself (use `cloud_create_app_build`) or to stop an ongoing rollout (pause the channel with `cloud_update_app_channel`).

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

appBuildId.description: The id of the build to deploy. For a rollback, the id of the last known good build. Use `cloud_list_app_builds` to look it up.

appChannelId.description: The id of the live update channel to deploy to. Provide either a channel or a destination.

appChannelName.description: The name of the live update channel to deploy to, e.g. "production". Alternative to `appChannelId`.

appDestinationId.description: The id of the app store destination to publish to. Provide either a channel or a destination.

appDestinationName.description: The name of the app store destination to publish to, e.g. "TestFlight". Alternative to `appDestinationId`.

rolloutPercentage.description: The share of devices that receive the live update, between 0 and 1, e.g. 0.1 for 10 percent. Defaults to 1 (everyone).

tools.name: cloud_update_app_deployment
tools.description: Change the rollout percentage of an existing live update deployment. Use this to widen a staged rollout once a build looks healthy, e.g. from 10 percent to 50 percent and then to 100 percent. Returns the updated deployment with its new `rolloutPercentage`. Do not use this to roll back: deploy the previous build with `cloud_create_app_deployment`, or pause the channel with `cloud_update_app_channel` to stop updates entirely. Lowering the percentage does not remove the update from devices that already received it.

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

deploymentId.description: The id of the deployment, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_app_deployments` to look it up.

rolloutPercentage.description: The new share of devices that receive the update, between 0 and 1, e.g. 0.5 for 50 percent.

tools.name: cloud_list_app_devices
tools.description: List the devices of an app in Capawesome Cloud that checked for live updates, most recently seen first. Use this to confirm that devices are reaching the update endpoint at all, to see which app versions are in the field, and to find the id of a tester's device. Returns `id`, `appChannelId`, `appDeploymentId`, `forcedAppChannelId`, `appVersionName`, `appVersionCode`, `platform` (0 = Android, 1 = iOS), `osVersion`, `pluginVersion`, `customId` and `lastSeenAt` per device. Do not use this to check whether one device would receive an update (use `cloud_probe_app_device`) or to count monthly active devices (see the usage view in the Capawesome Cloud Console).

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

id.description: Return only the device with this exact id. Optional.

query.description: A free-text filter matching the name or id, e.g. "production". Defaults to no filter.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return, e.g. 20. Defaults to 10, maximum 50.

offset.description: The number of items to skip, e.g. 10 to read the second page. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: cloud_get_app_device
tools.description: Get a single device of an app in Capawesome Cloud. Use this to inspect what a specific device reported: its app version, plugin version, operating system and the channel and deployment it is currently on. Returns `id`, `appChannelId`, `appDeploymentId`, `forcedAppChannelId`, `appVersionName`, `appVersionCode`, `platform` (0 = Android, 1 = iOS), `osVersion`, `pluginVersion`, `customId` and `lastSeenAt`. Do not use this to reason about the next update the device will receive: `cloud_probe_app_device` resolves the channel and deployment for you.

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

deviceId.description: The id of the device, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Devices report it themselves; use `cloud_list_app_devices` to look it up.

tools.name: cloud_probe_app_device
tools.description: Check which live update a device of an app in Capawesome Cloud would receive, and why it might receive none. Use this as the first step when a tester reports "the update never arrives": it resolves the channel the device is on (a forced channel wins over the channel the device reported), and reports whether that channel is paused, which deployment it serves and at what rollout percentage. Returns the resolved `channelName`, `channelPaused`, `deploymentId`, `rolloutPercentage`, the deployed `buildNumber`, plus the device's own `appVersionName`, `pluginVersion` and `lastSeenAt`. Note that this reads the current configuration instead of performing a real update check, so it does not consume usage or register the device. A rollout below 100 percent is decided per device, so a device inside the rollout may still be skipped. Do not use this to change the channel of a device: use `cloud_update_app_device`.

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

deviceId.description: The id of the device, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Devices report it themselves; use `cloud_list_app_devices` to look it up.

tools.name: cloud_update_app_device
tools.description: Force a device of an app in Capawesome Cloud onto a specific live update channel, or clear that override. Use this to put a tester's device on a "beta" channel without changing the app, and pass null to hand the device back to the channel the app itself requests. Returns the updated device with its `forcedAppChannelId`. Do not use this to change the channel for everyone: set the app's default channel with `cloud_update_app`. Do not use it to remove a device (use `cloud_delete_app_device`).

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

deviceId.description: The id of the device, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Devices report it themselves; use `cloud_list_app_devices` to look it up.

forcedAppChannelId.description: The id of the channel the device must use, or null to clear the override. Use `cloud_list_app_channels` to look the id up.

tools.name: cloud_delete_app_device
tools.description: Delete a device of an app in Capawesome Cloud. Use this to clean up stale records, e.g. a device that was wiped or handed to someone else. The record and its forced channel assignment are removed. Returns a confirmation. Do not use this to stop a device from receiving updates: an installed app registers again on its next update check, so clear or change its forced channel with `cloud_update_app_device` instead.

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

deviceId.description: The id of the device, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Devices report it themselves; use `cloud_list_app_devices` to look it up.

tools.name: cloud_list_app_environments
tools.description: List the environments of an app in Capawesome Cloud. An environment groups the variables and secrets a build runs with. Use this to resolve an environment name such as "staging" to its id before starting a build or editing its values. Pass `name` to filter by exact name, which returns the single match since environment names are unique. Returns `id`, `name`, `appId` and the timestamps per environment. Do not use this to read variable values (use `cloud_get_app_environment`) or to change them (use `cloud_update_app_environment`).

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

name.description: Filter by exact name, e.g. "production". Returns the single match, since names are unique. Optional.

query.description: A free-text filter matching the name or id, e.g. "production". Defaults to no filter.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return, e.g. 20. Defaults to 10, maximum 50.

offset.description: The number of items to skip, e.g. 10 to read the second page. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: cloud_get_app_environment
tools.description: Get a single environment of an app in Capawesome Cloud together with its variables and the keys of its secrets. Use this to check which values a build will see, and to find out whether a secret exists before overwriting it. Returns the environment `id` and `name`, the `variables` as key and value, and the `secretKeys`. Secret values are never returned by the API. Do not use this to change a value (use `cloud_update_app_environment`) or to pass one-off values to a single build (use `adHocEnvironmentVariables` of `cloud_create_app_build`).

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

environmentId.description: The id of the environment, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_app_environments` to look it up by name.

tools.name: cloud_create_app_environment
tools.description: Create an environment for an app in Capawesome Cloud. Use this to separate build configuration per stage, e.g. a "staging" and a "production" environment. Creation only takes a name: add the variables and secrets afterwards with `cloud_update_app_environment`, then reference the environment when creating a build. Returns the created environment with `id` and `name`. Do not use this to create an app configuration that overrides the native app id and name (use `cloud_create_app_configuration`).

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

name.description: The name of the environment, e.g. "staging".

tools.name: cloud_update_app_environment
tools.description: Rename an environment of an app in Capawesome Cloud and set or remove its variables and secrets. Use `setVariables` for plain configuration a build may print, and `setSecrets` for credentials, which are encrypted and masked in build logs. Existing keys are overwritten; keys listed in `unsetVariables` or `unsetSecrets` are deleted. Every change is dispatched as its own API call and reported individually, so a partial failure names the exact key that failed. Returns the applied and failed changes per key. SECURITY: any value passed to this tool becomes part of the conversation and is stored in the transcript. For production credentials use the Capawesome CLI or the Console instead, and use this tool only for values that may be exposed. Do not use this to pass a value to a single build only (use `adHocEnvironmentVariables` of `cloud_create_app_build`), and do not expect to read a secret back: the API never returns secret values.

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

environmentId.description: The id of the environment, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_app_environments` to look it up by name.

name.description: The new name of the environment, e.g. "staging". Optional.

setVariables.description: Non-secret variables to create or overwrite, e.g. { "API_URL": "https://staging.example.com" }. Optional.

setSecrets.description: Secrets to create or overwrite, e.g. { "SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN": "..." }. Values are encrypted and masked in build logs, but still travel through this conversation. Optional.

unsetVariables.description: Variable keys to delete, e.g. ["API_URL"]. Optional.

unsetSecrets.description: Secret keys to delete, e.g. ["SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN"]. Optional.

tools.name: cloud_delete_app_environment
