appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

gitConnectionId.description: The id of the Git connection, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_git_connections` to look it up.

path.description: The provider path of the repository, e.g. "acme/mobile-app". Take it from `cloud_list_git_repositories`.

tools.name: cloud_delete_app_repository
tools.description: Unlink an app in Capawesome Cloud from its Git repository. Use this when an app moves to another repository or should no longer be built from Git. Builds from a Git reference and automations stop working until a repository is linked again; nothing in the repository itself is touched. Returns a confirmation. Do not use this to switch repositories: `cloud_set_app_repository` replaces the link in one step. Do not use it to delete the Git connection (use `cloud_delete_git_connection`).

appId.description: The id of the app, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_apps` to look it up by name.

tools.name: cloud_list_jobs
tools.description: List the jobs of a Capawesome Cloud organization, newest first. A job is the unit of work behind a build or a deployment. Use this to see what is currently running or queued across all apps, e.g. with `status: ["queued", "in_progress"]` to check the build queue, or `["failed"]` to find recent failures. Returns `id`, `appId`, `status`, `stack`, `appBuildId`, `appDeploymentId`, `finishedAt` and `createdAt` per job. Do not use this to list builds or deployments themselves (use `cloud_list_app_builds` / `cloud_list_app_deployments`), and do not use it to read logs (use `cloud_diagnose_job`).

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

status.description: Return only jobs in these statuses, e.g. ["queued", "in_progress"]. Defaults to all statuses.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return, e.g. 20. Defaults to 10, maximum 50.

offset.description: The number of items to skip, e.g. 10 to read the second page. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: cloud_get_job
tools.description: Get a single job of Capawesome Cloud by its id. Use this to poll a build or deployment you started until its `status` leaves `queued`, `pending` or `in_progress`. Returns `id`, `appId`, `status`, `stack`, `appBuildId`, `appDeploymentId`, `finishedAt` and `createdAt`. Do not use this to find out why a job failed: `cloud_diagnose_job` returns the log tail and an explanation in one call.

jobId.description: The id of the job, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Builds and deployments expose it as `jobId`.

tools.name: cloud_cancel_job
tools.description: Cancel a job of Capawesome Cloud that has not finished yet. This is the single way to stop a running build or deployment — there is no separate cancel tool per resource. Use it when a build was started from the wrong branch or a deployment must not complete. Returns the job with its updated `status`. Do not use this on jobs that already finished, and do not use it to undo a completed deployment: deploy the previous build with `cloud_create_app_deployment` or pause the channel with `cloud_update_app_channel`.

jobId.description: The id of the job, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Builds and deployments expose it as `jobId`.

tools.name: cloud_diagnose_job
tools.description: Diagnose a Capawesome Cloud job by fetching the AI-generated summary of why it failed. Use this whenever a build or a deployment failed, before guessing at causes: the summary names the likely reason and how to address it. Returns the job `status` and the failure `summary`. The summary is only available for failed jobs. Do not use this to poll a running job (use `cloud_get_job`). The raw build log is not returned; read the complete log in the Capawesome Cloud Console.

jobId.description: The id of the job, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Builds and deployments expose it as `jobId`.

tools.name: cloud_list_license_keys
tools.description: List the license keys of a Capawesome Cloud organization. License keys unlock Capawesome Insiders packages: the Sponsorware plugins and the Enterprise SDKs (such as the Ionic Enterprise SDK replacements). They authenticate installs against the Capawesome npm registry. Use this to find the key a developer or CI job needs to install Insiders packages, or to check which key is about to expire. Returns `id`, `name`, `key`, `expiresAt`, `lockedUntil` and, with `includePackages`, the assigned packages per license key. Do not use this to manage the organization subscription, which is not exposed through this server. Treat the returned `key` as a credential.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

includePackages.description: Whether to include the packages the license key grants access to, e.g. true. Defaults to false.

tools.name: cloud_get_license_key
tools.description: Get a single license key of a Capawesome Cloud organization. License keys unlock Capawesome Insiders packages: the Sponsorware plugins and the Enterprise SDKs (such as the Ionic Enterprise SDK replacements). They authenticate installs against the Capawesome npm registry. Use this to read the key value for an `.npmrc` or a CI secret, and to check which Insiders and Enterprise SDK packages it unlocks. Returns `id`, `name`, `key`, `expiresAt`, `lockedUntil` and, with `includePackages`, the assigned packages. Do not use this to look a key up by its value: list the keys of the organization with `cloud_list_license_keys` instead. Treat the returned `key` as a credential.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

licenseKeyId.description: The id of the license key, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_license_keys` to look it up.

includePackages.description: Whether to include the packages the license key grants access to, e.g. true. Defaults to false.

tools.name: cloud_create_license_key
tools.description: Create a license key for a Capawesome Cloud organization. License keys unlock Capawesome Insiders packages: the Sponsorware plugins and the Enterprise SDKs (such as the Ionic Enterprise SDK replacements). They authenticate installs against the Capawesome npm registry. Use this to issue a separate key per environment or per team, e.g. one for local development and one for CI, so a leaked key can be rotated without disrupting everyone. Returns the created license key with `id`, `name`, `key` and the assigned packages. Treat the returned `key` as a credential. Do not use this to grant access to Capawesome Cloud itself: that is what organization members and teams are for. Requires an active Insiders subscription.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

name.description: The name of the license key, e.g. "CI pipeline".

packageIds.description: The ids of the packages the key unlocks. Defaults to the packages included in the subscription.

tools.name: cloud_update_license_key
tools.description: Update the name or the package assignments of a license key in a Capawesome Cloud organization. License keys unlock Capawesome Insiders packages: the Sponsorware plugins and the Enterprise SDKs (such as the Ionic Enterprise SDK replacements). They authenticate installs against the Capawesome npm registry. Use this to rename a key or to change which Sponsorware, Insiders and Enterprise SDK packages it unlocks. `packageIds` replaces the current assignment, so send the full list. Returns the updated license key. Do not use this to change the key value: rotate it with `cloud_rotate_license_key`. Packages cannot be changed while the key is locked — see `lockedUntil`.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

licenseKeyId.description: The id of the license key, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_license_keys` to look it up.

name.description: The new name of the license key, e.g. "CI pipeline".

packageIds.description: The complete list of package ids the key unlocks. Replaces the current assignment.

tools.name: cloud_rotate_license_key
tools.description: Rotate a license key of a Capawesome Cloud organization: a new key value is issued and the previous one stops working immediately. License keys unlock Capawesome Insiders packages: the Sponsorware plugins and the Enterprise SDKs (such as the Ionic Enterprise SDK replacements). They authenticate installs against the Capawesome npm registry. Use this as soon as a key leaked — for example when it was committed to a repository. Every install that still uses the old value fails right away, so update `.npmrc` files and CI secrets before or immediately after rotating. Returns the license key with its new `key` value. Do not use this to change package assignments (use `cloud_update_license_key`) or as a routine action: there is no way to recover the previous value.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

licenseKeyId.description: The id of the license key, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_license_keys` to look it up.

tools.name: cloud_delete_license_key
tools.description: Permanently delete a license key of a Capawesome Cloud organization. License keys unlock Capawesome Insiders packages: the Sponsorware plugins and the Enterprise SDKs (such as the Ionic Enterprise SDK replacements). They authenticate installs against the Capawesome npm registry. Use this for keys that are no longer needed at all. Installs of Sponsorware, Insiders and Enterprise SDK packages that use the key start failing immediately. Returns a confirmation. Do not use this to replace a leaked key: rotating with `cloud_rotate_license_key` invalidates the old value while keeping the key itself in place.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

licenseKeyId.description: The id of the license key, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_license_keys` to look it up.

tools.name: cloud_list_teams
tools.description: List the teams of a Capawesome Cloud organization. A team grants a group of members access to a group of apps. Use this to see how access is structured before adding someone to a project, and to resolve a team name to its id. Pass `name` to filter by exact name, which returns the single match since team names are unique. Returns `id`, `name`, `description`, `totalTeamApps`, `totalTeamMembers` and the timestamps per team. Do not use this to list all members of the organization (use `cloud_list_members`) or all apps (use `cloud_list_apps`).

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

name.description: Filter by exact name, e.g. "production". Returns the single match, since names are unique. Optional.

query.description: A free-text filter matching the name or id, e.g. "production". Defaults to no filter.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return, e.g. 20. Defaults to 10, maximum 50.

offset.description: The number of items to skip, e.g. 10 to read the second page. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: cloud_get_team
tools.description: Get a single team of a Capawesome Cloud organization, optionally including its apps and members. Use this to check who has access to which apps through a team, and to read the `teamAppId` and `teamMemberId` values that `cloud_update_team` needs to remove an assignment. Returns `id`, `name`, `description`, `totalTeamApps`, `totalTeamMembers` and, when requested, `teamApps` and `teamMembers` with their assignment ids. Do not use this to find a team by name: use `cloud_list_teams`.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

teamId.description: The id of the team, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_teams` to look it up by name.

includeApps.description: Whether to include the apps assigned to the team, e.g. true. Defaults to false.

includeMembers.description: Whether to include the members assigned to the team, e.g. true. Defaults to false.

tools.name: cloud_create_team
tools.description: Create a team in a Capawesome Cloud organization. Use this to scope access to a subset of apps, e.g. a "Mobile" team that only sees the customer app. Add apps and members afterwards with `cloud_update_team`. Returns the created team with `id`, `name` and `description`. Do not use this to invite people to the organization (use `cloud_create_invitation`) — only existing members can be added to a team.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

name.description: The name of the team, e.g. "Mobile".

description.description: A short description of what the team is for, e.g. "Customer facing apps". Optional.

tools.name: cloud_update_team
tools.description: Rename a team of a Capawesome Cloud organization and change which apps and members belong to it. Use `addAppIds` and `addMemberIds` to grant access, and `removeTeamAppIds` and `removeTeamMemberIds` to revoke it. Removals take the assignment id, not the app or member id: read them from `cloud_get_team` with `includeApps` and `includeMembers`. Every change is dispatched separately and reported individually, so a partial failure names the assignment that failed. Returns the applied and failed changes together with the refreshed team. Do not use this to change a member's organization role, which this server does not expose, and do not use it to remove someone from the organization entirely (use `cloud_delete_member`).

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

teamId.description: The id of the team, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_teams` to look it up by name.

name.description: The new name of the team, e.g. "Mobile". Optional.

description.description: The new description of the team. Pass null to clear it.

addAppIds.description: The ids of apps to grant the team access to, from `cloud_list_apps`. Optional.

removeTeamAppIds.description: The `teamAppId` values of app assignments to remove, from `cloud_get_team` with `includeApps`. Optional.

addMemberIds.description: The membership ids to add to the team, from `cloud_list_members`. Optional.

removeTeamMemberIds.description: The `teamMemberId` values of member assignments to remove, from `cloud_get_team` with `includeMembers`. Optional.

tools.name: cloud_delete_team
tools.description: Permanently delete a team of a Capawesome Cloud organization. Use this when a team is no longer needed. Its members lose the access the team granted them, but stay members of the organization. Returns a confirmation. Do not use this to remove a single app or member from a team: `cloud_update_team` removes individual assignments.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

teamId.description: The id of the team, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_teams` to look it up by name.

tools.name: cloud_list_git_connections
tools.description: List the Git connections of a Capawesome Cloud organization. A connection holds the credentials Capawesome Cloud uses to clone repositories for builds. Use this to find the connection id needed to browse repositories or to link a repository to an app, and to spot broken connections — `brokenAt` is set once the stored credentials stopped working. Returns `id`, `name`, `provider`, `authKind`, `baseUrl`, `restricted`, `brokenAt`, `lastUsedAt` and the timestamps per connection. Tokens and passwords are never returned. Do not use this to list repositories (use `cloud_list_git_repositories`) or to see which repository an app uses (use `cloud_get_app_repository`).

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

provider.description: Return only connections for this provider, e.g. "github".

name.description: Return only the connection with this exact name, e.g. "Acme GitHub".

query.description: A free-text filter matching the name or id, e.g. "production". Defaults to no filter.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return, e.g. 20. Defaults to 10, maximum 50.

offset.description: The number of items to skip, e.g. 10 to read the second page. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: cloud_get_git_connection
tools.description: Get a single Git connection of a Capawesome Cloud organization. Use this to check whether a connection still works before blaming a failing build on something else: `brokenAt` is set when the stored credentials were rejected. Returns `id`, `name`, `provider`, `authKind`, `authUsername`, `baseUrl`, `restricted`, `brokenAt`, `lastUsedAt` and the timestamps. Tokens and passwords are never returned. Do not use this to test access to a specific repository: list the repositories with `cloud_list_git_repositories`.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

gitConnectionId.description: The id of the Git connection, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_git_connections` to look it up.

tools.name: cloud_create_git_connection
tools.description: Create a Git connection for a Capawesome Cloud organization using an access token or basic authentication. Use `authKind: "token"` with a personal access token that may read the repositories to build, or `authKind: "basic"` with a username and password for self-hosted servers. Set `baseUrl` for a self-hosted provider. Returns the created connection with `id`, `name`, `provider` and `authKind`; pass that id to `cloud_list_git_repositories` and `cloud_set_app_repository`. SECURITY: any value passed to this tool becomes part of the conversation and is stored in the transcript. For production credentials use the Capawesome CLI or the Console instead, and use this tool only for values that may be exposed. Do not use this for OAuth or GitHub App connections: those require an interactive authorization flow and must be created in the Capawesome Cloud Console.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

authKind.description: How the connection authenticates: "token" for a personal access token, "basic" for username and password.

name.description: The name of the connection, e.g. "Acme GitHub". Defaults to a name derived from the provider.

baseUrl.description: The base URL of a self-hosted provider, e.g. "https://git.acme.com". Defaults to the provider cloud offering.

token.description: The access token, required for `authKind: "token"`. Grant it read access to the repositories only.

tools.name: cloud_update_git_connection
tools.description: Update a Git connection of a Capawesome Cloud organization, typically to store a rotated token or password. Use this when `brokenAt` is set or a credential expired. Changing `authKind` or `baseUrl` requires sending the matching credential along in the same call. Returns the updated connection. SECURITY: any value passed to this tool becomes part of the conversation and is stored in the transcript. For production credentials use the Capawesome CLI or the Console instead, and use this tool only for values that may be exposed. Do not use this to convert a connection to OAuth or a GitHub App: create those in the Capawesome Cloud Console instead.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

gitConnectionId.description: The id of the Git connection, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_git_connections` to look it up.

name.description: The new name of the connection, e.g. "Acme GitHub".

authKind.description: The new authentication kind, e.g. "token". Send the matching credential along.

baseUrl.description: The new base URL of a self-hosted provider, e.g. "https://git.acme.com". Pass null to use the provider cloud offering.

tools.name: cloud_delete_git_connection
tools.description: Permanently delete a Git connection of a Capawesome Cloud organization. Use this when a connection is no longer needed or its credentials must be revoked. Apps whose repository is linked through this connection can no longer be built from Git. Returns a confirmation. Do not use this to rotate a credential: update the connection with `cloud_update_git_connection`, which keeps every repository link intact.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

gitConnectionId.description: The id of the Git connection, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_git_connections` to look it up.

tools.name: cloud_list_git_repositories
tools.description: List the repositories a Git connection of a Capawesome Cloud organization can access. Use this to find the exact repository `path` that `cloud_set_app_repository` expects, and to verify that the connection really reaches a repository before linking it. Returns `id`, `name`, `namespace`, `path` (e.g. `owner/name`), `private`, `webUrl` and `defaultBranch` per repository. Do not use this to read repository contents or commits: Capawesome Cloud only clones repositories during builds. For Azure DevOps a `namespace` of the form `organization/project` is required.

organizationId.description: The id of the organization, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_organizations` to look it up.

gitConnectionId.description: The id of the Git connection, e.g. "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000000". Use `cloud_list_git_connections` to look it up.

namespace.description: The namespace to list repositories of, e.g. "acme". Required for Azure DevOps as "organization/project".

path.description: Look up a single repository by its provider path, e.g. "acme/mobile-app". Optional.

query.description: A free-text filter matching the repository name, e.g. "mobile".
